name: Bolandiol
lead: Bolandiol (19-nor-4-androstenediol, estr-4-ene-3beta,17beta-diol) is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid related to nandrolone. The base compound was never marketed as a drug, though its dipropionate ester (anabiol) has been sold [1]. Bodybuilders who discussed it, mostly in the prohormone era of the early 2000s, were interested in it as a nandrolone-like compound that could add lean mass and so improve physique [8][11].

Animal research describes it as unusual among anabolic steroids because it has androgenic, estrogenic and progestational activity. In castrated adult male rats it increased lean mass and bone mineral density without strongly stimulating sex accessory glands [2]. Wikipedia states that several clinical studies concluded it did not change strength, body composition or exercise performance, although the human studies it cites examined closely related compounds [1].
The World Anti-Doping Agency lists it as prohibited [1], and norandrostenediol isomers appeared in US legislative text on anabolic steroids that T Nation members discussed in 2004 [12].

paras: Bolandiol is a 3-beta,17-beta-diol analogue related to nandrolone, lacking the C19 methyl group of testosterone-type steroids. Related compounds include 19-nor-4-androstenedione (bolandione), 19-nor-5-androstenediol and 4-androstenediol [1]. Forum members distinguished Nandrosol, a spray containing 19-nor-4-androstene-3,17-diol, from Androsol, which contained 4-androstenediol [10].

A 2010 study found bolandiol bound the androgen receptor with lower affinity than testosterone, dihydrotestosterone, nandrolone or estradiol, with low but measurable affinity for progestin and estrogen receptors. It stimulated transcription through each receptor, though at only 4-9 percent of the potency of the reference androgens in the assays described, and it suppressed gonadotropins and endogenous testosterone production [2]. It may be metabolised to nandrolone or a related compound [1][7]. Earlier rat work compared its effect on prostate androgen receptor levels with those of androgens, antiandrogens and other anabolic steroids [3].

A 2008 method-validation study measured 19-nor-4-androstenediol and its metabolites in plasma after six healthy men took two capsules of a commercial prohormone supplement (Norandrodiol Select 300), sampling for 24 hours; the authors describe it as a prohormone of nandrolone [7].

A T Nation poster in 2000 recalled that the 19-nor compound was patented by G.D. Searle in the 1960s and esterified as the dipropionate bolandiol, as a veterinary steroid, and described early comparisons with nandrolone decanoate [9]. Another 2002 poster noted that it had been sold as an anabolic steroid in other countries before use as a supplement [8]. These are forum accounts.

In the early 2000s, over-the-counter prohormone supplements containing norandrostenediol were sold in the United States and discussed in long T Nation threads [11]. In 2004, forum members posted legislative text listing norandrostenediol isomers among anabolic steroids under debate [12]. UK forum users listed 19-norandrostenedione among newly banned substances in 2008 [13]. The World Anti-Doping Agency lists bolandiol among prohibited substances [1].

Bolandiol has been used as a comparison compound in animal models for evaluating selective androgen receptor modulators; a 2013 study compared gene expression across tissues after treatment with dihydrotestosterone and bolandiol at 16 hours and 6 weeks [4]. A guinea pig MRI study in castrated animals examined growth effects of four over-the-counter steroid precursors, including bolandiol [5]. A 1981 rat study of bolandiol dipropionate examined its effect on diethylnitrosamine-induced liver tumours; tumour numbers were increased in the group treated after the carcinogen [6].

No clinical trial of bolandiol itself was found. Wikipedia summarises older clinical studies as showing no change in strength, body composition or performance, but the human trials it cites examined the related prohormones 19-nor-4-androstenedione and 19-nor-4-androstenediol [1]. Other human data consist of the single-dose pharmacokinetic study of a supplement [7].

lore.intro: Bolandiol appears in T Nation discussions of prohormones and their legal status in the 2000s [11][12].

claims.believers: Forum posters described the compound as virtually identical to nandrolone when given orally, citing the old Searle patent [9].
claims.experts: Rat research shows mixed androgen, estrogen and progestin activity with low androgen receptor affinity [2], and the clinical studies summarised on Wikipedia reported no change in strength or body composition [1].

claims.claim: Topical sprays deliver the prohormone effectively
claims.believers: Posters compared Nandrosol and Androsol sprays and discussed their ingredients [10].
claims.experts: No trial of topical delivery was found.

card.summary: A nandrolone-related steroid with mixed androgen, estrogen and progestin activity; studied in rats, never marketed as a base.
card.note: WADA-prohibited; reported to show no strength or body-composition effect in clinical studies per Wikipedia.

quick.overview:
Bolandiol is a nandrolone-like anabolic steroid. Its dipropionate ester has been marketed in the past, but the base compound never was.

In castrated rats it raised lean mass and bone density. Wikipedia reports clinical studies found no change in strength, body composition or performance.
quick.mechanism: It binds the androgen receptor weakly but also has estrogenic and progestational activity, and it suppresses gonadotropins and endogenous testosterone.
quick.risks: It suppresses natural testosterone production in animals. It is on the WADA prohibited list.

chain: Metabolised to or acting like a nandrolone-type steroid
Androgen receptor activation in muscle and bone
Lean mass gains sought by users
angle.text: Prohormone users discussed bolandiol as a precursor of nandrolone that could build muscle for a more muscular physique. Rat studies report increased lean mass and bone density with it [2], while the human studies summarised on Wikipedia reported no change in strength or body composition [1].
